content:
Apple finally responds to the surge in memory and other component costs, taking a notably hard line. Some price hikes exceed fifty percent, while certain memory and storage upgrades have effectively doubled in price.

Such steep pricing could very well persist for years — or even indefinitely…

9to5Mac readers had already been sceptical about whether Apple would roll back prices once component supply pressures eased. More than two-thirds of respondents expect these increases to be permanent.

Subsequent analyst reports indicate that supply chain pricing will not improve in any meaningful way before 2028, and even then, any improvement is likely to be minimal. Today's exceptionally high prices appear set to last for years at the very least, and quite possibly forever.

If that scenario plays out, how will you respond? Will you grit your teeth and keep buying Apple products at the same pace? Cut back on quantity or frequency? Or adopt other strategies — such as choosing cheaper models, buying refurbished units, or waiting for discounts before pulling the trigger?

You're welcome to cast your vote and share your thoughts in the comments. Multiple selections are allowed if you intend to change your purchasing behaviour in more than one way.
